question.worked_solution:
We will write the equation of the line in the slope-intercept form 

$$
y=mx+b.
$$

As we found previously, the slope is $m=-\frac{1}{3}.$

Substituting $m=-\frac{1}{3}$ into the slope-intercept form above, we get

$$
y=-\frac{1}{3}x+b.
$$

We now need to find the $y$-intercept $b.$ We can find this by substituting the coordinates of a point on the line. Any point will do, so let's substitute $(4,1):$

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =-\frac{1}{3}x+b \\ 1 & =-(\frac{1}{3})(4)+b \\ 1 & =-\frac{4}{3}+b \\ 1+\frac{4}{3} & =b \\ b & =\frac{7}{3}\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the equation of the line is 

$$
y=-\frac{1}{3}x+\frac{7}{3}.
$$

From the picture, the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-2,3)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(4,1),$ respectively.

To find the length of $\overset{―}{AB},$ we use the distance formula:

$$
\begin{aligned}|\overset{―}{AB}| & =\sqrt{({x}_{2}-{x}_{1})^{2}+({y}_{2}-{y}_{1})^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(4-(-2))^{2}+(1-3)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{(6)^{2}+(-2)^{2}} \\  & =\sqrt{36+4} \\  & =\sqrt{40} \\  & =2\sqrt{10}\end{aligned}
$$

As we found previously, the points $A$ and $B$ have coordinates $({x}_{1},{y}_{1})=(-2,3)$ and $({x}_{2},{y}_{2})=(4,1),$ respectively.

Therefore, we compute the slope $m$ of the line as follows:

$$
